title: Finite jets at a fixed point detect the kernel of an algebraic action
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $H$ be a separated finite-type $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with no affineness, smoothness or connectedness assumption. Let $X$ be a smooth connected separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Suppose $a:H\times_kX\to X$ is an action, meaning that $a(1,z)=z$ and $a(h,a(h',z))=a(hh',z)$ after every base change, with products as in [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $x:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ be fixed by this action, meaning $a\circ(\mathrm{id}_H\times x)=x\circ p_H$. Write $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ for the local ring (the stalk of the structure sheaf), and $\mathfrak m=\ker(R\to k)$ for its maximal ideal. For $n\geq1$ put $V_n=R/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$, with ideal powers and quotient rings in their usual ring-theoretic sense [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Then $V_n$ is a nonzero finite-dimensional $k$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. Pullback by the inverse action on the infinitesimal neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}V_n\hookrightarrow X$ defines a homomorphism of $k$-group schemes $\rho_n:H\to\operatorname{GL}(V_n)$; here $\operatorname{GL}(V_n)$ is the affine general linear group [def-sc-general-linear-group] in any basis, whose $B$-points are the invertible $B$-linear maps of $B\otimes_k V_n$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Its scheme-theoretic kernel $K_n=H\times_{\operatorname{GL}(V_n)}\operatorname{Spec}k$ is a closed normal finite-type subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup, def-weil-closed-immersion]. There is $n_0\geq1$ such that for every $n\geq n_0$, every commutative $k$-algebra $B$, and every $h\in H(B)$, one has
$$h\in K_n(B)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a_{B'}(h_{B'},z)=z\ \text{for every commutative }B\text{-algebra }B'\text{ and every }z\in X(B').$$
Thus a single sufficiently high jet detects the entire action kernel on all algebra-valued points, including nonreduced algebras.

source.place: Proposition 8.9 proof, printed p.150: descending kernels on O_P/m_P^(n+1) and Krull intersection; use its argument up to identifying the stable kernel with the kernel of the action, before invoking faithfulness. Fixed subschemes: Theorem 7.1, printed pp.138--139. Smooth connected X over an algebraically closed field ensures that X is reduced and irreducible, as required in the fixed-subscheme argument. Corollary 8.10 is the conjugation application. No Stacks tag states this action-kernel theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-rational-point-thickenings-base-change] to $(X,x)$. Thus $R$ is Noetherian local with residue $k$, each $V_n$ is nonzero finite-dimensional, and $Z_n=\operatorname{Spec}V_n\subset X$ has ideal $\mathcal J^{n+1}$. For every $k$-scheme $T$, its base change is the thickening of the section $x_T$ defined by $\mathcal J_T^{n+1}$. Smoothness gives regularity by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular]. The rational point makes $X$ nonempty; connectedness and [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral] therefore make $X$ integral. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], with base $\operatorname{Spec}k$, makes $H$ Noetherian. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0,k$.

source.place: Proposition 8.9, printed p.150, local quotients and Noetherianity; reducedness correction in the appended errata. Stacks 056S, 0569, 033N, 01T6 supply the cited geometric inputs.

proof.text: For a $k$-scheme $T$ and $h:T\to H$, the action defines the $T$-automorphism $c_h$ of $X_T$, $z\mapsto h z$, with inverse $c_{h^{-1}}$. Since $x$ is fixed as a morphism, $c_h$ preserves the section $x_T$, hence its ideal $\mathcal J_T$ (the kernel of restriction to the section) and all its powers. Step 1 therefore restricts $c_h$ to $T\times Z_n$. For $T=\operatorname{Spec}B$, pullback by $c_{h^{-1}}$ is a $B$-algebra automorphism $T_h$ of $B\otimes_kV_n$. It is natural in $B$. The identity $c_{(hh')^{-1}}=c_{h'^{-1}}c_{h^{-1}}$ and contravariance give $T_{hh'}=T_hT_{h'}$, and $T_1=1$. The restriction maps $V_{n+1}\to V_n$ commute with these operators because the same automorphism preserves both ideal powers.

source.place: Proposition 8.9, first paragraph: action on infinitesimal neighbourhoods; inverse-action convention made explicit.

proof.text: This construction works for every $k$-scheme $T$, not just affine ones: on affine charts the coordinate modules of $T\times Z_n$ are $\mathcal O_T\otimes_kV_n$ by step 1, and the pullbacks agree on overlaps. In a basis of $V_n$, its automorphism $T_h$ is an invertible matrix of sections, hence, by [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction] (morphisms $T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ correspond naturally to ring maps $A\to\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$, and $k$-morphisms to $k$-algebra maps), a $T$-point of the general linear group $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of [def-sc-general-linear-group], whose $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$-points are the invertible matrices; this description is basis-independent as an automorphism of the free module. We have a natural transformation $h_H\to h_{\operatorname{GL}(V_n)}$ on all $k$-schemes. [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful], with category $(\mathit{Sch}/k)$, gives a unique morphism $\rho_n$. The identities of step 2 make it a group-scheme homomorphism. The cited GL description applies since $\dim_kV_n\geq1$.

source.place: Proposition 8.9, first paragraph, natural representations and Yoneda; Stacks 001P (categories-lemma-yoneda).

proof.text: By [lem-sc-kernel-subgroup], $K_n=\ker\rho_n$ is a closed subgroup with $K_n(B)=\ker\rho_n(B)$ for every $k$-algebra $B$. These kernels are normal: $\rho_n(ghg^{-1})=\rho_n(g)1\rho_n(g)^{-1}=1$ for $h\in K_n(B)$, universally in $B$. Closed subschemes of a finite-type $k$-scheme are finite type: intersect a finite affine cover with the closed subscheme; its coordinate rings are quotients of finitely generated $k$-algebras. Since $V_{n+1}\to V_n$ is surjective after every scalar extension, equivariance in step 2 gives $K_{n+1}(B)\subseteq K_n(B)$ for all $B$. Test on affine charts of $K_{n+1}$ to obtain a factorization $K_{n+1}\to K_n$ over $H$, equivalently an inclusion $\mathcal L_n\subseteq\mathcal L_{n+1}$ of their quasi-coherent ideal sheaves.

source.place: Proposition 8.9, descending kernels; elementary kernel and closed-immersion ideal calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-acc-quasi-coherent] on the Noetherian scheme $H$ to the nonempty set $\{\mathcal L_n:n\geq1\}$ of quasi-coherent ideals. Choose a maximal member $\mathcal L_{n_0}$. Since the sequence is increasing, maximality forces $\mathcal L_n=\mathcal L_{n_0}$ for all $n\geq n_0$. Thus $K_n=K_{n_0}$ as closed subschemes, including nilpotents. Put $K=K_{n_0}$. The inclusions also imply $K\subseteq K_n$ for every $n\geq1$. Hence the restricted $K$-action on each $Z_n$ is trivial: its inverse pullback on functions is the identity on every algebra point, so the action morphism equals the projection, tested on affine charts of $K\times Z_n$.

source.place: Proposition 8.9, descending-chain stabilization as closed subgroup schemes; Stacks 01Y8 (coherent-lemma-acc-coherent).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-universal-fixed-subscheme] to the restriction of the action to $K\times X$. Its hypotheses hold: $K$ is separated and finite type as a closed subscheme of $H$, and $X$ is separated finite type. Let $Y=X^K\hookrightarrow X$ have quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I$. The trivial actions on $Z_n$ and the fixed-subscheme factorization property give $Z_n\subseteq Y$ for every $n\geq1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-factor-ideal-inclusion], $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal J^{n+1}$, so $\mathcal I_x\subseteq\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ for every $n$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson] to $R$, its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and the cyclic module $R$. The maximal ideal of a local ring is its Jacobson radical. The intersection is zero; omitting the exponents $0,1$ leaves the same intersection by nesting. Consequently $\mathcal I_x=0$.

source.place: Theorem 7.1, printed pp.138–139; Proposition 8.9, ideal and Krull intersection paragraph. Stacks 01QP and 00IQ (algebra-lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module), part (2).

proof.text:
The equality $\mathcal I_x=0$ forces $\mathcal I=0$ because $X$ is integral. Here are the affine details. Take an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $x$. If $t\in\mathcal I(U)$, then $t/1=0$ in $A_{\mathfrak p_x}$, so $st=0$ for some $s
otin\mathfrak p_x$. The domain $A$ has $s
e0$, hence $t=0$, and $\mathcal I|_U=0$ by quasi-coherence. For any nonempty affine $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$ in $X$, irreducibility makes $W\cap U$ nonempty. Choose a nonempty principal open $D(f)\subset W\cap U$. For $t\in\mathcal I(W)$ its image in $C_f$ is zero, so $f^rt=0$ for some $r$. Since $C$ is a domain and $f
e0$, $t=0$. Thus $\mathcal I$ vanishes on every affine, $Y=X$, and the fixed-subscheme statement says that $K	imes X	o X$ equals the projection.

source.place: Proposition 8.9, final fixed-subscheme argument, with the reducedness gap repaired by the integral affine calculation (errata p.2).

proof.text: Fix $n\geq n_0$, a commutative $k$-algebra $B$, and $h\in H(B)$. If $h\in K_n(B)=K(B)$, the equality of action and projection on $K\times X$ remains an equality after any $B$-algebra extension $B'$, proving $a_{B'}(h_{B'},z)=z$ for every $z\in X(B')$. Conversely suppose this universal condition holds. For the affine chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}C$ of $X_B$, test it at the point of $X(C)$ given by $U\hookrightarrow X_B\to X$, taking $B'=C$. It gives $c_h|_U=\mathrm{id}|_U$. These charts cover $X_B$, so $c_h=\mathrm{id}$, and its inverse has identity pullback on $B\otimes_kV_n$. Thus $\rho_n(B)(h)=1$, or $h\in K_n(B)$. No reduction of $B$ or $B'$ entered this argument.
